methodological_rigor.justification: This is a retrospective EHR-based cohort study from the UC Health Data Warehouse (January 2021 to January 2025) including 12,360 adults with multiple myeloma, of whom 320 (2.6%) received CAR-T (Abstract). The design is appropriate for describing associations between demographic/clinical factors and CAR-T receipt, but causal interpretation is limited by confounding (e.g., referral patterns, eligibility nuances) and missingness in key severity measures (ISS unknown in 7.5% due to missing labs) (Abstract; Methods 2.4). Statistical modeling uses a generalized linear model/logistic regression adjusted for age, gender, ADI, insurance, location, CRAB features, ISS stage, race, and ethnicity (Methods 2.5), but the manuscript does not fully resolve unmeasured clinical and social determinants that drive access.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is an individual observational cohort analysis of treatment receipt patterns within a large health system, consistent with Oxford LoE 2b (Abstract). The question is highly clinically relevant because CAR-T availability is constrained and disparities in access can affect outcomes in relapsed/refractory myeloma (Importance/Introduction). The findings that CAR-T receipt varied by treatment location and that Black or African American patients had lower odds of receiving CAR-T than White patients (OR 0.33; 95% CI 0.17–0.62) (Abstract) have direct implications for care pathways and equity interventions, even though the study does not evaluate clinical efficacy.

reporting_quality.justification: STROBE applies to this retrospective cohort study, and the manuscript reports the data source, dates, cohort size, covariates, and the adjusted regression framework used to estimate odds ratios (Abstract; Methods 2.4–2.5). The LLM sub-study describes inclusion/exclusion for the UCSF notes cohort (270 patients; 417 notes) and a zero-shot, temperature-0 prompting approach with clinician-validated subsample testing (Methods 2.6). However, detailed performance metrics for the LLM validation and complete code/data sharing are not provided in the blinded text, limiting reproducibility. Data availability appears constrained to the described warehouse and supplements rather than open release.

novelty_literature.justification: While disparities in access to advanced therapies are a well-studied theme, this work adds novelty by combining a large multi-site health system cohort with a targeted LLM-based clinical-note assessment of whether CAR-T was discussed and whether eligibility was documented (Abstract; Methods 2.6). The use of zero-shot GPT inference on Assessment & Plan sections to classify eligibility and discussion status is a relatively novel operational approach within this context. Overall, the contribution is more innovative on methods/measurement than on biological or therapeutic novelty.

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is detailed and quantitative, stating cohort size, time window, key adjusted associations (ORs with CIs), and the LLM note-review component. Methods define covariates clearly (ADI, ISS, CRAB features, insurance, race/ethnicity, location) and specify the adjusted modeling approach (Methods 2.4–2.5). The limitations section explicitly discusses temporal changes in CAR-T indications, missing ISS components, and limitations of neighborhood-level socioeconomic proxies and note-based capture of discussions (Discussion/Limitations).

key_strengths: Large, multi-site real-world cohort (n = 12,360) spanning six academic centers and affiliated hospitals with a clear access-outcome (CAR-T receipt) (Abstract).
Adjusted modeling that includes both clinical severity proxies (ISS stage, CRAB features) and structural factors (UC location, insurance, ADI) (Methods 2.4–2.5).
Innovative LLM-based note review to identify potentially eligible patients without documented CAR-T discussions, with clinician-reviewed validation on a subsample (Methods 2.6).
key_concerns: Residual confounding and measurement limitations (e.g., eligibility criteria details, referral pathways, caregiver/social constraints) limit causal claims about inequity drivers (Discussion/Limitations).
Missingness in staging inputs (ISS unknown for some due to missing beta-2 microglobulin/cytogenetics) may bias severity adjustment and comparisons across sites (Abstract; Limitations).
LLM validation is described qualitatively; stronger reporting of performance metrics and error analysis is needed to support the note-based eligibility/dicussion conclusions (Methods 2.6).
chief_reviewer.rationale: The study is high-impact in topic and scale and includes a novel measurement layer via LLM note review, but it needs major revisions focused on confounding, missingness, and transparent LLM validation to support Tier 2 acceptance.
